moat_against: Efficiency laggard vs Old Dominion (79.9% record OR vs mid-70s benchmark); convergence is execution, not entitlement
Cyclical industrial freight: Q2 2026 tonnage per day only +1% YoY; volume recovery unproven
Structural capex intensity: FY2026 guided gross capex $500-600M; conservative OE was negative in FY2023-24
Leverage and European drag: net debt $2,943M = 5.7x TTM OE; European segment posted a Q2 2026 operating loss
moat_for: Scale and density: ~9% U.S. LTL share, ~300 service centers, 99% ZIP coverage
Scarce terminal footprint: 28 Yellow terminals bought for $870M; dock-door capacity +15% since 2021
Consolidated, pricing-disciplined industry post-Yellow; yield ex-fuel +4.4% YoY in Q2 2026
Proprietary tech and insourcing: outsourced linehaul miles 25.2% (2020) to 6.1% (Q2 2026); record <0.2% damage claims ratio
moat_justification: LTL density and scarce terminal real estate are genuine advantages and the post-Yellow industry is consolidated and pricing-disciplined, but XPO still trails Old Dominion on efficiency (record 79.9% adjusted OR vs mid-70s benchmark), freight is cyclical with tonnage only +1% YoY in Q2 2026, and the network consumes structural capex every year; leverage is 5.7x TTM OE and the European segment dilutes the story.
name: XPO, Inc.
one_liner: Strong LTL network, moat 6/10, margins inflecting — but at $188.83 the OE yield is 2.28% and even the super-bull case returns only 9.8%; it clears 15% only near $50.30, so Tier D.
